notes: Dev TBox expansion paired with biology-replace-d005 (every shark has a skeleton made of cartilage -> bone): the revised rule's new conclusion (a skeleton made of bone, relation skeleton_made_of) given to a made-up class under a real one (Drellidae, a newly described marine family), fictional: subject. Revision and expansion both end in 'bone'; only the revision has to push cartilage out. The real superclass is 'marine animal' rather than 'fish' on purpose: most fish are bony, so for a new fish family 'bone' (and osteoblasts) would be the default guess without the edit; marine animals have no default skeleton (shells, chitin, cartilage, bone, none), so the answers need the edit. A made-up class has no member the model already knows, so the first derived question states a made-up membership in the prompt (a specimen that taxonomists placed in Drellidae) and asks what its skeleton is made of: inheritance, 2 hops, as the other topics' dev TBox expansions do (review: a TBox expansion must test that the rule reaches a member). The other two derived questions are compositions that follow the rule to bone and look up a stored fact about bone (each bridge checked before editing): the mineral that gives it hardness (hydroxyapatite) and whether it matches the adult human skeleton (yes; 'mainly' because the human skeleton has some cartilage). Review: the earlier 'which cell breaks down skeletal tissue' question (osteoclasts) was guessable without the edit, since 'breaks down' and 'skeletal tissue' point to osteoclasts by default (they also resorb calcified cartilage); the mineral question is open, names no tissue, and bone and cartilage give different answers (cartilage has no such mineral). Guess-rate caveat, left to the model audit: 'skeleton' plus a family name may lead a model to guess 'bone' without the edit, since most vertebrate families are bony; the marine-animal superclass is kept because it has no default skeleton, but pre-edit answer rates of the direct, paraphrase, inheritance and mineral questions should be read from the audit before this record is trusted. Evidence for the new facts reuses the record's own zero-hit counts for Drellidae and adds counts for the bone-mineral bridge (856 for 'bone hydroxyapatite', 538 for 'hydroxyapatite in bone'). Near unrelated asks the skeleton of a stingray, a real marine animal outside the class whose answer (cartilage) differs from the new one, so a rule that leaks to marine animals in general is caught (Rule 7). The name has the zoological family ending '-idae' and no root that suggests a skeleton. Re-check on 2026-11-12: every infini-gram count in the six biology contraction and expansion records was asked again (47 distinct queries across the six records, 0 mismatched); Wikipedia quotes are copied from the revision records or from the articles' first sentences, and the Wikipedia search API answered HTTP 429 when this revision was written, so no new search could be run. Revision 2026-11-12 (model audit): Llama and Mistral answered 'Calcium' to the bridge check 'Which mineral gives bone most of its hardness?' (expected hydroxyapatite), so the hydroxyapatite derived question and its bridge were replaced: the derived question now asks whether a Drellidae skeleton would show up clearly on an ordinary X-ray (yes under bone; a cartilage skeleton would not), bridge 'Bone shows up clearly on X-ray images' (check: 'Does bone show up clearly on X-ray images?'), backed by the Radiography article and the hits above (all small; the claim rests on the quote).
